newsitem.title: USA: Two Illinois counties pass property tax limits.
newsitem.headline: Two Illinois counties pass property tax limits.

text.p: Voters in Illinois counties of McDonough and Stephenson approved property tax limitations in Tuesday's election, according to county clerks' offices.
Voters in three other counties, however, rejected the move. Those counties were Adams, McLean and Shelby, the county offices reported.

The measure limits annual increases in local government property tax collections to five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less. It also prohibits the issuance of general obligation bonds without voter approval.

Tax caps imposed by the Illinois General Assembly are already in effect in six Chicago-area counties. A 1996 Illinois law allowed the remaining 96 counties in the state to place the limitation measure on the ballot.
Last November, voters in 18 counties approved capping property taxes.
